entities.summary: A commercial confederation of merchant guilds and market towns (c. 1150–1669) that dominated Baltic and North Sea trade for over three centuries. At its peak involving ~200 cities from London to Novgorod, the Hansa controlled trade in fish, grain, timber, furs, and textiles. It pioneered multinational commercial law, standardized weights and measures, and created the model for future trading blocs.
